pull_request.title: Design: assess LAr gap and hadron-collider granularity options
pull_request.head: codex/lar-gap-hadron-options
pull_request.body:
The matched10k LAr study shows a weak barrel/endcap handover. This design input separates channel-service savings from the current800mm cryogenic routing reservation and compares mitigations for a possible hadron-collider use case.

- Proposes selective layer/region coarsening, endpoint-defined side/rear egress, coupled barrel/endcap coverage and residual-gap instrumentation.
- Reproduces existing service budgets: half/quarter planning channels reduce assumed electronics power but retain the739.403mm utility bend. Adds a clearly labelled straight-ray envelope screen;200/400mm inward shifts are unengineered scenarios that conflict with the existing route and forward reservation.
- Retains the limitations of the raw10k observable: lossless cell regrouping preserves its all-cell energy sum, and it does not establish calibrated hadron-collider superiority.
- Records separate pinned SysArch/PhysVal inputs, primary FCC-hh provenance, work identification and disjoint observed token logging. No detector geometry or approval state changes.

Validation:3 existing service controls pass; screening JSON reproduces byte-identically; analytic endpoint/bend checks, PNG inspection, project/session/inventory and token-site validation pass. No native geometry, engineering route or shower validation was run.

Related: PR75 transition review; merged PR138/139 placement campaign and PR14010k comparison. Draft for technical discussion; no design acceptance or merge authorization inferred.
